newsitem.title: USA: Investors get shot at Zell office REIT.
newsitem.headline: Investors get shot at Zell office REIT.

text.p: Part of the largest publicly traded office building owner in the country is expected to begin trading Tuesday, attracting investor attention because of its broad mix of properties and the pricing of the deal.
The fact that the company, Equity Office Properties Trust, is controlled by high-profile financier Samuel Zell also may be attracting some interest.

"People say it's the star quality of Zell," said Kenneth Campbell, chairman of CRA Real Estate Securities, a money management firm dealing in real estate securities. "I think it's really a vision of a company that is in scale and scope like nothing that's really come down the pike."

The offering has been rumoured for as long as a year and is expected to receive a strong reception, analysts said. It is expected to be priced late Monday at the upper end of the $19-to-$21 range quoted in the prospectus.
In terms of scale, Equity Office's portfolio includes 90 office properties totalling about 32.2 million square feet. The portfolio also includes 14 stand-alone parking lots.

In 1996, the company's predecessors had $508.1 million in revenues, according to prospectus materials for the offering. The company has the largest office portfolio, in terms of revenues and square feet, of any publicly traded company in the country, the prospectus said.

The real estate investment trust, or REIT, had about $1.6 billion in debt as of March 31 and its properties were 92.5 percent occupied as of April 30. Proceeds from the offering are to be used to pay down debt.

In terms of scope, the properties are in 47 markets, giving it a national profile, unlike most of the larger REITs that are mostly regional in nature, said Robert Natale, analyst at Standard & Poors Equity Group.
REITs, which pay out most of their taxable income to shareholders to preserve their special tax status, are also an attractive place for investors who focus on total return, Natale said.

Analysts noted that Zell has a strong track record with two other real estate investment trusts: Equity Residential Properties Trust, an apartment REIT, and Manufactured Home Communities Inc, an operator of mobile home communities. Zell is chairman of all three REITs.
"People think Zell is able to buy things at attractive prices," said David Linn, analyst at McDonald & Co. Securities.

The offering of 25 million shares represents about 15.6 percent of the company. That diminishes the liquidity one would associate with the largest office REIT, said John Fosheim, a principal with Green Street Advisors, an independent REIT research firm in Newport Beach, California.

But Fosheim also said he expected the issue to trade above the $19-to-$21-a-share range in the after-market, noting that the expected offering price barely represents any premium on underlying net asset value, while other office REITs trade at 30 percent premiums of net asset value.
"It represents good value at this price," he said.
